title: A phase IV randomised, parallel-group, double-blinded, placebo-controlled, trial evaluating the efficacy of the tree SLIT-tablet in adolescents (12-17 years of age) with allergic rhinitis/allergic rhinoconjunctivitis induced by birch pollen using an environmental exposure unit.
official: A phase IV randomised, parallel-group, double-blinded, placebo-controlled, trial evaluating the efficacy of the tree SLIT-tablet in adolescents (12-17 years of age) with allergic rhinitis/allergic rhinoconjunctivitis induced by birch pollen using an environmental exposure unit.
summary: Main objective: To compare the efficacy of the tree SLIT-tablet to placebo after at least 16 weeks of treatment of moderate to severe AR/ARC induced by birch pollen in adolescents (12-17 years of age)
conditions: Moderate to severe allergic rhinitis/allergic rhinoconjunctivitis induced by birch pollen
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Written informed consent obtained from parents/caregivers before any trial related procedures are performed. Consent or assent from the participant must be obtained according to national requirements
2. Male or female aged 12 to 17 years on the day of the randomisation visit
3. A female participant of childbearing potential must have a negative pregnancy test and be willing to practice appropriate contraceptive methods until the last follow-up visit (TC4)
4. A documented, physician diagnosed, clinically relevant history of moderate to severe AR/ARC induced by birch pollen (with or without asthma) despite having received treatment with symptom-relieving medication during at least 2 previous tree pollen seasons at screening
5. Positive specific immunoglobulin E (IgE) (defined as ≥IgE Class 2; ≥0.7 kU/L) against Bet v within the past 12 months prior to screening
6. Positive SPT (wheal size of ≥5 mm) to Bet v within the past 12 months prior to screening
7. Minimum level of rhinoconjunctivitis symptoms, defined as a TSS of at least 7 (of 18) and TNSS of at least 6 (of 12), at one timepoint during the birch baseline EEU session
8. The participant must be willing and able to comply with the trial protocol
Exclusion criteria:
1. Previous participation in this trial. Participation is defined as randomisation
2. Acute severe oral inflammation
3. Any nasal or naso/oropharyngeal condition that could confound the efficacy or safety assessments (e.g., hypertrophy of the pharyngeal/palatine tonsils, clinically relevant nasal polyps, a history of paranasal sinus surgery or surgery of nasal turbinates)
4. A diagnosis of eosinophilic oesophagitis
5. A relevant history of systemic allergic reaction, e.g. anaphylaxis with cardiorespiratory symptoms, generalised urticaria or severe facial angioedema that in the opinion of the investigator may constitute an increased safety concern
6. Any clinically relevant chronic disease incl. malignancy that in the opinion of the investigator would interfere with the trial evaluations or the safety of the participant
7. Active or poorly controlled autoimmune diseases, immune defects, immunodeficiencies, immunosuppression or malignant neoplastic diseases with current disease relevance
8. Immunosuppressive treatment (ATC code L04 or L01) within 90 days prior to the screening visit
9. Treatment with medications with potential impact on efficacy endpoints. For example, treatment with anti-IgE drugs within 130 days/5 half-lives of the drug (whichever longest) prior to randomisation
10. Treatment with an investigational drug within 30 days/5 half-lives of the drug (whichever longest) prior to screening
11. Is participating or planning to participate in any other interventional clinical trial during the duration of this trial
12. Has a clinically relevant history of symptomatic (seasonal or perennial) AR/ARC caused by an allergen source other than tree pollen from the birch homologous group, and where the allergen source is expected to be present during the periods where the participant is attending EEU challenges
13. A history of allergy, hypersensitivity, or intolerance to the IMP (except to the active ingredient) or any of the background treatment provided in this trial
14. Female who is pregnant or breast-feeding
15. Has a business or personal relationship with trial staff or sponsor who is directly involved with the conduct of the trial
16. Another person from the trial participants’ household is participating in the trial, e.g. siblings or spouses must not be enrolled in the trial at any given time
17. Cannot cooperate or complete trial procedures/manoeuvres
18. A history of alcohol or drug abuse
19. Asthma requiring medium or high daily doses of inhaled corticosteroids (asthma treatment step 4 or 5 according to GINA guidelines (GINA Executive Committee 2024)) within 3 months prior to the randomisation visit
20. A known history of birch or tree pollen induced asthma exacerbation
21. Within the last 3 months before the randomisation visit, has had an occurrence of any clinical deterioration of asthma (i.e. asthma exacerbation) that resulted in emergency treatment, hospitalisation, or treatment with systemic corticosteroids
22. Reduced lung function at screening, baseline EEU session (V2) or randomisation (V3) defined as FEV1 <70% of predicted value. For participants with asthma, FEV1 is assessed on participants’ usual asthma medication following at least a 6-hour wash-out of SABA
23. SLIT treatment with pollen allergen extracts from birch and trees belonging to the birch homologous group for more than 1 month within the last 5 years. In addition, any SLIT treatment with birch pollen or cross-reactive/homologous tree pollen allergen extracts within the previous 12 months
24. SCIT treatment with pollen allergen extracts from birch and trees belonging to the birch homologous group reaching the maintenance dose within the last 5 years. In addition, any SCIT treatment with birch pollen or cross-reactive/homologous tree pollen allergen extracts within the previous 12 months
25. Ongoing treatment with any allergy immunotherapy product
